name: Improbable Traverse

pitch_detail.notes: Initial low to mid-5th class climbing through loose, crumbly rhyolite terrain; lots of holds but quality poor and exposed
Continuation of crumbly terrain leading toward Lunch Ledge; climbers should carefully test all holds
Final approach to Lunch Ledge (~300 ft from start); large comfortable belay ledge provides good rest point before upper pitches

The iconic Improbable Traverse pitch(es): traverse right on good foot ledges with several old fixed pitons for protection. Critical: November 2021 rockfall destroyed ~30x40ft section; now requires downclimbing 5.9-5.10 from old pin with 30+ feet of unprotected traversing. Many now recommend this route is not safe.
Class 4 ramp climbing through alpine trees and rock slabs to summit ridge approach; short but exposed

rappels: No rappels on the climb itself. The descent over the summits requires one ~30 m rappel from a slung tree on the east side below the middle summit into the SE couloir; parties who lose the line or get benighted have reported using up to four tree rappels. Carry a 60 m rope, extra webbing and rap rings.
descent_text: After summiting via Improbable Traverse, most climbers traverse north over Guye's north and middle summits to descend via established gully systems. A climbers' trail descends from the Guye-Snoqualmie saddle area. For faster/safer descent, fixed anchors (tree with rap tatters) provide rappel opportunity on east side of summit to bypass exposure. Southeast Couloir descent toward Cave Ridge parking is viable alternative.
approach: From Alpental Ski Area parking lot (3,120 ft), reach the talus cone below the west face by a line that stays off the private Alpental Community Club roads; the 'Strasse' roads off the access road are closed to walking and driving, and no established path exists. Approach time ~30 minutes to 1 hour from parking.
overview: A technical alpine rock climb on Guye Peak's prominent west face offering a classic 5.8 traverse pitch with stellar views from Interstate 90. Once popular, the route was heavily damaged by rockfall in November 2021; current conditions are marginal and downclimbing on the traverse is now required.
beta: Start from Alpental parking lot and reach the talus cone by a line that avoids the private Strasse roads (no established path). Scramble ~200 feet of loose, mossy, dirty slabs to reach first anchor. Climb 6 pitches of mixed alpine rock through crumbly terrain to Lunch Ledge at ~300 feet. The iconic traverse (pitches 4-5) traverses right on good ledges with old fixed pitons; now requires careful downclimbing due to 2021 damage. Upper pitches climb Class 4 ramp terrain with trees and exposure to summit. Route is sustained and exposed throughout; not a beginner alpine rock climb.
fa: Dave Hiser and Mike Borghoff, 1960; first winter ascent Kit Lewis, 1975
